lessons.title: From peach baskets to the shot clock
lessons.objective: Place Naismith, the BAA/NBA merger and the 24-second clock.

payload.prompt: Put basketball history milestones in order.

items.text: BAA founded as pro basketball league

explanation.correct: Perfect. Basketball grew from a YMCA exercise to the pro game over 60+ years.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Basketball started 1891, pro league 1946, merger 1949, shot clock 1954.

payload.prompt: Why did Naismith invent basketball?

options.text: To give athletes an indoor sport for winter.
To replace football as America's favorite sport.
To create a game for professional players.

explanation.correct: Right. Naismith wanted indoor winter exercise. He nailed it.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Basketball started as a practical winter sport, not as pro entertainment.

payload.prompt: What did the NBA start as?

options.text: The BAA, founded 1946 and merged with the NBL in 1949.
A direct spinoff of college basketball.
A league that started in 1954.

explanation.correct: Exactly. The BAA became the NBA after absorbing the NBL.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. NBA history: BAA 1946, merger 1949, then growth from there.

payload.prompt: What problem did the 24-second shot clock solve?

options.text: Games were slowing down; teams stalled to protect leads.
Players were scoring too many points.
Refs needed time to make calls.

explanation.correct: Right. Before 1954, teams could hold the ball forever. Shot clock saved the game.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Early pro basketball had no time limit on possessions, so games died.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Basketball is actually pretty young as a sport.

payload.question: What is she noting?

options.text: Modern basketball is only about 130 years old, newer than many sports.
Basketball players are younger than football players.
The game changes every season.
Most players retire young.

payload.translation: She means basketball started in 1891, making it newer than baseball and football.

followUps.line: That explains why the game changed so much.
followUps.why: Good recognition that younger sports evolve faster than established ones.

followUps.line: American game, basically.
followUps.why: Fair observation that Naismith's invention became an American institution.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Basketball is genuinely young: 1891 is only 135 years ago. Baseball and football started earlier.

lessons.title: Russell, Wilt and the 1960s
lessons.objective: Explain the Celtics dynasty and the first big-man era.

payload.prompt: What made the Celtics dynasty so rare?

options.text: 11 titles in 13 years with Bill Russell; no team has matched that dominance.
They won in the 1960s when basketball was new.
Russell was the first professional player.

explanation.correct: Right. Celtics' 11 in 13 is unmatched. Russell's defense and team play set a standard.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The Celtics won 11 titles from 1957-1969, a record nobody else comes close to.

payload.prompt: Why was the 1960s a big-man era?

options.text: Wilt and Russell dominated; centers were the most important players.
Centers were the only players allowed to score.
The court was bigger in the 1960s.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Wilt's scoring and Russell's defense made centers the game's core.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The 1960s featured dominant centers like Wilt and Russell at the peak.

payload.prompt: Match 1960s basketball concepts.

pairs.definition: 11 titles in 13 years (1957-1969) led by Bill Russell; defensive principles and team play.
1960s dominated by centers Wilt and Russell; post-centric basketball and individual dominance.
Russell's innovation: help and rotation, not just individual shot-blocking.

distractorDefinitions: A fast-paced offense with multiple ball handlers.
A style where all players shoot from distance.

explanation.summary: Celtics won through team defense. Russell pioneered help-side rotations. Wilt represented individual dominance.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Russell has more rings than anyone. Nobody else even comes close.

payload.question: What is the context?

options.text: Bill Russell won 11 NBA championships, mostly with the Celtics, a record unmatched.
Russell wore more jewelry than other players.
Russell invented the ring in basketball.
Russell's rings are more valuable than others'.

payload.translation: She's pointing out that Russell's 11 titles stand alone. No modern player has won half that many.

followUps.line: That is crazy when you think about it.
followUps.why: Good reaction recognizing how dominant a run 11 championships is.

followUps.line: Different era though, fewer teams.
followUps.why: Valid observation: fewer teams in the 1960s made championships easier to win.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Russell's 11 titles is fact. Fewer teams existed then, but the dominance over 13 years is still historic.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Wilt and Russell were like aliens playing against regular humans.

payload.question: What is she describing?

options.text: Wilt and Russell were so much better physically than their peers.
They wore strange uniforms.
They came from another country.
They played in space.

payload.translation: She means Wilt's athleticism and Russell's defense gave them superhuman advantages in the 1960s.

followUps.line: Yeah, Wilt was a freak.
followUps.why: Fair description of Wilt's unprecedented athletic ability.

followUps.line: Modern players would still be amazing then.
followUps.why: Good point that current athletes are better trained and stronger overall.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Wilt's scoring and athleticism, plus Russell's defense, were exceptional for the era.

lessons.title: Magic, Bird and the 1980s
lessons.objective: Explain why the 1980s built the modern league.

options.text: Their rivalry and games brought fans back during an era when the league was struggling.
They were the first players to ever score points.
They invented the three-pointer.

explanation.correct: Right. Magic's Lakers vs Bird's Celtics was must-watch TV. It saved the NBA.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The Magic-Bird rivalry in the 1980s revived fan interest when the NBA was in trouble.

A game show that replaced basketball.
Boring defensive basketball.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Showtime meant fast breaks, passing and fun. Fans loved it.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Showtime was the Lakers' style: quick, flashy passes and fast-break scoring.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: The Bad Boys Pistons made basketball rough in the late 1980s.

payload.question: What is she describing?

options.text: Detroit's physical, aggressive defensive style that won championships.
A rock band that played at games.
Players who fouled out every game.
A team with bad sportsmanship.

payload.translation: She means the Pistons' bruising defense and physical play defined their identity.

followUps.line: They won because of it.
followUps.why: Correct: Bad Boys' physical defense won back-to-back titles (1989-1990).

followUps.line: Rules are stricter now.
followUps.why: Good observation: modern defensive rules limit the contact the Pistons used.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Bad Boys (1989-1990 Pistons) won through intense, physical team defense; different rules now.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: The 1980s had Magic and Bird on TV constantly. It was the best.

payload.question: Why was that significant?

options.text: Magic and Bird's rivalry brought mainstream attention to the NBA when viewership was low.
They were the only two players in basketball.
They had the most points ever.
TVs were invented in the 1980s.

payload.translation: She means the Magic-Bird Finals matchups and rivalry became must-watch television.

followUps.line: Different eras now; social media changes things.
followUps.why: Fair observation that modern stars reach audiences differently.

followUps.line: But that rivalry was pure basketball.
followUps.why: Good recognition that the 1980s rivalry was about the game itself.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Magic-Bird rivalry (1980s) was transformative for the NBA; their Finals meetings were iconic.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Showtime was exciting because nobody knew what was coming next.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: Lakers played flashy, improvised offense with quick passes and fast breaks.
Showtime was a magic trick.
The Lakers were on television every night.
The game had no rules.

payload.translation: She means Showtime basketball was unpredictable: Magic could pass from anywhere, fast breaks came from nowhere.

followUps.line: That is fun to watch.
followUps.why: Valid: modern analytics-heavy ball is more predictable.

followUps.line: Still need defense though.
followUps.why: Good point that Showtime worked because they could also defend.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Showtime relied on Magic's vision, quick passing, and willingness to take risks on fastbreaks.

lessons.title: Jordan, the Dream Team and going global
lessons.objective: Explain the Bulls dynasty and the 1992 Olympic team.

payload.prompt: How many titles did Jordan win?

options.text: Six championships in eight years (1991-1998), three-peat twice.
10 titles; he never lost.
One title, then he retired.

explanation.correct: Right. Jordan's six titles in eight years is the modern standard for greatness.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Jordan won six: 1991-1993 and 1996-1998, two three-peats.

payload.prompt: What was special about the 1992 Dream Team?

options.text: NBA all-stars (Jordan, Magic, Bird, etc.) dominated the Olympics as amateurs, changing global game.
It was a team of high school players.
It lost a game in the Olympics.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Dream Team was the first Olympic team with NBA stars. They won by huge margins.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Dream Team featured NBA pros and dominated 1992 Olympics, promoting the game worldwide.

payload.prompt: How did the Dream Team change basketball?

options.text: Exposed the world to NBA talent; international players later joined the league.
It invented three-pointers.
It changed the rules of basketball.

explanation.correct: Right. Dream Team inspired global interest. International basketball grew after 1992.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Dream Team showed the world NBA-level basketball, inspiring international talent to pursue the league.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Six titles in eight years, and he never came back like everyone else did.

payload.question: What is she noting?

options.text: Jordan retired while still at his peak, keeping his legacy clean.
Jordan never returned to the NBA.
Jordan played eight seasons total.
Jordan never played basketball again.

payload.translation: She means Jordan quit while still dominant (after 1993 and again after 1998), unlike many stars who decline.

followUps.line: Yeah, he went out on top.
followUps.why: Exactly: Jordan ended on his terms, in his prime.

followUps.line: But he did come back briefly.
followUps.why: Fair correction: Jordan had minor returns but not a full rebuild like others.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Jordan won his last title in 1998, then retired (mostly) at 35, while still elite.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: The Dream Team showed the world what real basketball looked like.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: NBA stars demonstrated elite-level basketball on the Olympic stage to a global audience.
It was literally a dream.
Nobody had ever played basketball before.
The Olympics invented basketball.

payload.translation: She means the Dream Team's dominance and style set the standard for basketball globally.

followUps.line: Changed how the game was played everywhere.
followUps.why: True: Dream Team influenced international basketball development.

followUps.line: Still got dominated in some countries.
followUps.why: Fair: some international programs were competitive even then.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Dream Team (1992) is widely credited with globalizing basketball and inspiring international talent pipelines.

lessons.title: Shaq, Kobe, Duncan and LeBron

explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Lakers and Spurs were the dynasties: Lakers 2000-2002, Spurs 2003 onward.

payload.prompt: When did LeBron change the game?

options.text: 2003 onward; he redefined positionless basketball and modern athleticism.
LeBron never changed anything.
LeBron started in 1991.

explanation.incorrect: Not quite. LeBron's arrival (2003) marked the shift to positionless basketball.

lessons.title: Curry, the Warriors and the three

Three-pointers were never popular.

Curry only shoots threes.
